Warm-up, no script: what would you tell a business owner who says 'we're on Google, we're fine'?
interview: MEAT 1 · THE TOP THREE — Here's what's happening. Someone grabs their phone and types 'roofer near me.' Google shows a map with three businesses on it. Those three get the calls. Everybody else is down below, and most people never make it that far. So it doesn't matter how good your work is. If you're not one of those three, you don't exist to that customer. The good news? Google picks those three based on stuff you control: your Google profile, your reviews, your website. Fix those, and you start showing up where the money is.

MEAT 2 · REVIEWS — When someone's choosing between you and the shop down the street, they read your reviews first. How many you have. How recent they are. And whether you answered them. One of my clients, a tour company in Scottsdale, has over a thousand Google reviews at 4.9 stars, and every single one has a reply. Customers see that. Google sees that. And they're number one for 'Scottsdale off road.' So here's your move: ask every happy customer for a review, and answer every single one. Good or bad.

MEAT 3 · THE WEBSITE LEAK — Even when people find you, your website can lose them in seconds. They're on their phone. If the page is slow, or they can't find your number, your prices or your hours, they hit back and call the next guy. You never even know they were there. A restaurant I work with went from about 13,900 Google clicks a year to over 35,000. Same restaurant. Same food. Way more people finding them. Your website should be your best salesperson. Right now it might be your quietest.

MEAT 4 · CHATGPT — People aren't just Googling anymore. They're asking ChatGPT, 'Who's the best plumber in Vegas?' And it doesn't hand back ten options. It names a few. If your info online is thin, outdated, or says something different everywhere, it names somebody else, and that customer never even sees you. Try it today. Open ChatGPT, type 'best,' plus what you do, plus your city. If your name's not in the answer, that's a customer you just lost. The fix: make sure everywhere you show up online tells the same clear story about who you are.

MEAT 5 · THE PROOF — Let me show you what fixing this looks like. Desert Dog runs off-road tours in Scottsdale. In the last twelve months, people saw them on Google more than 880,000 times. That's three and a half times the year before. Clicks to their website, up 76%. They're number one for 'Scottsdale off road,' with over a thousand reviews at 4.9 stars. No tricks. We got the basics right: their Google profile, their reviews, their website. And we kept doing it every single month. That's the whole game. Be the business people find, trust and call.
